title: Test spatial composition with multiple objects
description: Generate test images with explicit spatial relationships (e.g., 'object A to the left of object B', 'character blocking doorway', 'item in foreground'). Evaluate how reliably OmniGen2 places objects where specified. Include tests for: foreground/background placement, left/right/center positioning, blocking/occlusion relationships, relative size.
notes:
## Spatial Composition Test Results

Tested OmniGen2's ability to handle explicit spatial relationships. All 5 test categories passed.

### Test Results
- 01_left_right: Lantern left, sword right - PASS
- 02_center: Jade figurine centered on altar - PASS  
- 03_foreground_background: Lantern foreground, archway background - PASS
- 04_blocking: Troll blocking doorway - PASS
- 05_relative_size: Tiny mouse vs giant boots - PASS

### Findings
Strengths: Left/right/center positioning, foreground/background depth, blocking/occlusion, and relative size comparisons all work reliably.

### Conclusion
OmniGen2 handles spatial composition well for text adventure illustration. No additional tools (GLIGEN, ControlNet) appear necessary for basic spatial positioning.

title: Evaluate OmniGen2 scene composition and reference-based consistency
description: Systematically test OmniGen2's ability to: (1) reliably compose scenes with multiple objects in specified spatial relationships, (2) use reference images to maintain consistency of characters, objects, and style across generations. This will determine if we need additional tools like GLIGEN/ControlNet or if OmniGen2 alone is sufficient.

title: Test object count accuracy
description: Test how reliably OmniGen2 generates the correct number of objects when specified (e.g., 'three candles', 'two guards'). This is a known weakness of diffusion models.

title: Test small object visibility in complex scenes
description: The jade figurine was missing/hard to see in the Hades scene. Test various approaches: stronger emphasis in prompt, foreground placement language, larger relative size descriptions. Determine if small important objects can be reliably rendered.

title: Create reference image library for key objects
description: Generate and curate reference images for recurring Zork objects: brass lantern, elvish sword, jade figurine, trophy case, mailbox, etc. These will be used to test in-context generation for consistency.

title: Test in-context generation with reference images
description:
Use OmniGen2's native multi-image input to test: (1) style transfer from a reference, (2) object consistency using reference images, (3) combining multiple references (style + object). Measure how faithfully the reference is reproduced.

title: Test cross-scene consistency without references
description: Generate the same object/character in multiple different scenes using only text prompts (no reference images). Measure visual drift. This establishes the baseline for how much reference images help.

title: Evaluate if additional tools needed (GLIGEN, ControlNet, etc.)
description: Based on composition and consistency test results, determine if OmniGen2 alone is sufficient or if we need to add: GLIGEN for bounding box layout control, ControlNet for structural guidance, IP-Adapter for stronger reference adherence, StoryDiffusion for cross-scene consistency.

title: Add reference image support to test script
description: Extend test_omnigen2.py to accept --reference-image arguments for in-context generation testing. Support multiple references with prompt syntax like 'the lantern from <img1>'.
